newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Draft would seek to curtail Israel's role at U.N..
newsitem.headline: Draft would seek to curtail Israel's role at U.N..

text.p: A proposed resolution circulated by Arab states on Tuesday would seek to curtail Israel's participation in the General Assembly and call on U.N. members to bar the import of any goods produced or manufactured at settlements in Israeli-occupied territory.
It would also request U.N. members to take measures to halt any support for Israeli settlements and their economic infrastructures by companies and individuals in their respective countries.

The draft, still subject to negotiation, is being prepared for a resumed emergency special of the General Assembly prompted by a recent U.N. report that Israel had not abandoned construction of a settlement on occupied territory south of Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
No date has yet been set for the Assembly session, requested Monday by Egypt as current chairman of the Arab group, but it is expected to be around July 15.
The General Assembly, in an April 25 resolution, demanded that Israel immediately halt work on a housing project at Har Homa/Jabal Abu Ghneim, captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

It also demanded a halt to all other Israeli settlement activities, called for an end to all support for "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories, and asked Secretary-General Kofi Annan to report back within two months.

His report, published last week, said Israel had not abandoned its construction work and that this was "viewed as particularly serious" for a variety of political, geographic, demographic and economic reasons, as well as because of its effects on the faltering Middle East peace process.

Without saying how Israel's participation in the Assembly might be affected, the proposed draft would stress that "normal participation by a member state in the workings of the General Assembly cannot be caried out while it simultaneously and systematically violates international law, the provisions of the Charter of the United Nations and relevant United Nations resolutions."
The draft would also condemn Israel's failure to comply with the original demand to halt work on the controversial building project and repeat that demand.

Other provisions would recommend the holding of a conference by parties to the Fourth Geneva Convention, which bars settlements in occupied territory, to ensure respect for the convention. The secretary-general would be asked to provide U.N. facilities for such a conference.
The Assembly's emergency session would again be adjourned temporarily, subject to another recall.
